```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 9, fig.height = 6)
```

This synthetic example follows a predeclared development workflow. No external
outcome selects a model, threshold, feature or tuning parameter. The display
functions read saved results only; they do not calculate missing metrics or
recalibrate predictions. All plotted values are descriptive, without inferred
confidence intervals. These synthetic thresholds are not clinical advice.

```{r preparation}
library(stormbreaker)
predictors <- c("gene_a", "gene_b")
thresholds <- c(0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.5, 0.7)
```

## Binary: develop, lock, predict, evaluate

Declare the candidates and thresholds before viewing external outcomes. The
first pipeline is the predeclared illustrative final model, not a CV winner.

```{r binary-development}
development <- bi_example(120, seed = 1)
task <- bi_task(development, "patient_id", "outcome", predictors,
                       decision_thresholds = thresholds)
pipelines <- list(sb_pipeline(learner = "logistic"),
                  sb_pipeline(learner = "gaussian_naive_bayes"))
cv <- compare_cv(task, pipelines, folds = 3, seed = 1)
result_table(cv, metric = "roc_auc")
final_models <- lapply(pipelines, function(p) fit_final(task, p))
```

Supply only IDs and predictors to prediction. Endpoint construction and
external evaluation happen afterwards. Evaluation matches the exact patient
ID set and preserves endpoint order; it does not rely on row positions.

```{r binary-external}
external <- bi_example(100, seed = 2)
external$patient_id <- paste0("EXT_", external$patient_id)
external_x <- external[c("patient_id", predictors)]
predictions <- lapply(final_models, function(fit) {
  predict_final(fit, external_x, id_col = "patient_id")
})
endpoint <- bi_endpoint(external, "patient_id", "outcome")
evaluation <- eval_external(predictions[[1]], endpoint)
comparison <- compare_external(predictions, endpoint)
result_table(evaluation, metric = "roc_auc", cohort_label = "Synthetic binary cohort")
result_table(comparison, metric = "brier_score", cohort_label = "Synthetic binary cohort")
result_table(comparison, "runs", cohort_label = "Synthetic binary cohort")
```

The cohort label is supplied by the caller for display, not discovered from
patient IDs or certified as independent by this function. An omitted label is
missing in the table. A comparison represents one cohort; do not combine
unrelated cohorts in an artificial comparison object. CV fold-aware metrics
and pooled external metrics retain their different saved definitions.

```{r binary-plots}
if (requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) {
  print(plot_perf(cv, "roc_auc"))
  print(plot_perf(comparison, "roc_auc", cohort_label = "Synthetic binary cohort"))
  print(plot_calib(comparison, cohort_label = "Synthetic binary cohort"))
  print(plot_dca(comparison, cohort_label = "Synthetic binary cohort"))
}
```

## Survival: repeat at a predeclared horizon

Harrell C describes the saved risk ordering, not a horizon-specific
probability metric. The calibration and DCA plots separately use the
predeclared six-month prediction horizon.

```{r survival-workflow}
survival_development <- surv_example(120, seed = 1)
survival_task <- surv_task(
  survival_development, "patient_id", "time", "event", predictors, "month",
  prediction_horizon = 6, decision_thresholds = thresholds
)
survival_pipeline <- sb_pipeline()
survival_cv <- run_cv(survival_task, survival_pipeline, folds = 3, seed = 1)
survival_final <- fit_final(survival_task, survival_pipeline)
survival_external <- surv_example(100, seed = 2)
survival_external$patient_id <- paste0("EXT_", survival_external$patient_id)
survival_prediction <- predict_final(
  survival_final, survival_external[c("patient_id", predictors)], id_col = "patient_id"
)
survival_endpoint <- surv_endpoint(
  survival_external, "patient_id", "time", "event", "month", prediction_horizon = 6
)
survival_evaluation <- eval_external(survival_prediction, survival_endpoint)
result_table(survival_cv, metric = "harrell_c")
result_table(survival_evaluation, metric = "harrell_c",
                cohort_label = "Synthetic survival cohort")
result_table(survival_evaluation, "runs")
```

```{r survival-plots}
if (requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) {
  print(plot_perf(survival_evaluation, "harrell_c",
                             cohort_label = "Synthetic survival cohort"))
  print(plot_calib(survival_evaluation, cohort_label = "Synthetic survival cohort"))
  print(plot_dca(survival_evaluation, cohort_label = "Synthetic survival cohort"))
}
```

## Failure visibility and patient privacy

A metric status is separate from the complete evaluation status. Failed,
incomplete and nonfinite rows remain in the table; default performance plots
omit their labels. Set `show_unavailable = TRUE` for diagnostic labels without
points. An all-unusable display explicitly reports no usable results.
`sb_failure_table(evaluation)` and `sb_export_failures(evaluation,
"new-failures.csv")` retain saved issues separately; review error text before
sharing. A failed evaluation that saved
no metric has status `not_saved` and an `NA` estimate, not zero. Evaluation
errors and patient-match status are retained. There are no invented CV folds
in external `runs`: each row describes an evaluation.

```{r failure-example}
bad_prediction <- predictions[[1]]
bad_prediction$predictions$patient_id[1] <- "ID_NOT_IN_ENDPOINT"
failed_evaluation <- eval_external(bad_prediction, endpoint)
result_table(failed_evaluation, metric = "roc_auc")
result_table(failed_evaluation, "runs")
if (requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) {
  print(plot_perf(failed_evaluation, "roc_auc",
                            cohort_label = "Synthetic ID mismatch demonstration"))
}
```

`result_table(evaluation, "predictions")` returns saved **scored** external
rows, including outcomes; it does not return outcome-blind prediction input.
Review patient identifiers and outcomes before exporting or sharing. Failed
evaluations with no scored rows produce an empty prediction table; inspect
`runs` to see their failure. Bootstrap uncertainty and cross-cohort synthesis
retain their existing dedicated interfaces.

## Saved fixed-horizon survival scores

```{r external-horizon-metrics}
for (metric in c("time_auc", "uno_c", "ipcw_brier")) {
  print(result_table(survival_evaluation, metric = metric,
                       cohort_label = "Synthetic survival cohort"))
}
if (requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) {
  print(plot_perf(survival_evaluation, "time_auc",
                           cohort_label = "Synthetic survival cohort"))
}
```

The saved horizon and unit are retained even when the endpoint did not repeat
a horizon already present in the saved metric. Different targets remain
separate labels, not converted or pooled. Missing metrics from failed results
remain `not_saved`; a successful horizon-free result has `not_requested` for
these absent metrics. No survival curve, metric or confidence interval is
calculated by the display functions. IPCW Brier estimates above one remain
visible rather than being forced into a zero-to-one plotting range.

## Whole composite results

Tables, performance/calibration/DCA plots, reports and failure exports accept
whole repeated CV, IECV and stacking CV results. Context columns identify
`repeat_id`, `heldout_cohort_id`, `model_role`, `validation_scheme` and `view_id`.
A `view_id` identifies a structural saved entry, not a patient. Existing
pipeline IDs remain unchanged. Repeated stacks retain member/stack roles.
IECV is method-development validation, not final independent external
validation. No averaging or pooling across repeats or cohorts is performed.

```{r composite-saved-results}
composite_data <- bi_example(60, seed = 5)
composite_task <- bi_task(
  composite_data, "patient_id", "outcome", "gene_a"
)
composite_result <- sb_compare_repeated_cv(
  composite_task, list(sb_pipeline(learner = "logistic")),
  folds = 3, seeds = c(1, 2)
)
result_table(composite_result, metric = "roc_auc")
sb_failure_table(composite_result)
if (requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) {
  plot_perf(composite_result, "roc_auc")
}
```

Pass the same whole object to `sb_render_report()` with a new HTML filename;
each saved leaf gets a separate section. Pass a native `sb_run_stack_cv()` or
`sb_run_internal_external_cv()` result in exactly the same way. Stack views
show outer-CV members and the stack, not inner training folds. Failed entries
remain in tables and failure exports; default plots omit unavailable entries.
Different survival horizons and units remain distinct targets.
